tldr: The complete-data shrinking-common-core-width frontier for a causal dose derivative is the headline question: how do minimax risk and uniformly honest expected interval length depend jointly on \(n\) and \(w_n\) when all covariates and outcomes are observed? The primitive benchmark retains unknown Lipschitz interval supports, a common bounded measurable density shape, and additive outcomes with a bounded measurable covariate nuisance. Known protocol envelopes, \(C^3\) responses restricted only by the known slope envelope \(G_1\) and third-derivative envelope \(G_3\), and known unit Gaussian noise are deliberate restrictions; response intercepts are unrestricted. Buffered pilot extrema and a balanced cellwise-extrema construction give total finite-sample honest procedures and the improved complete-data upper bracket \(\mathfrak R_n\lesssim\min\{\mathfrak U_n,\mathfrak B_n\}\), with honest expected length bounded by \(\sqrt{\min\{\mathfrak U_n,\mathfrak B_n\}}\), while the classical lower endpoints remain \(n^{-4/7}\) and \(n^{-2/7}\). Extrema-conditioned reuse of the support-certification sample is also achievable at the buffered rates. The sharp moving-support converse and the frontier for the unresolved width regimes remain open.
gap: Interior-based and cross-fitted causal derivative theorems do not determine the complete-data shrinking-width information frontier on the exact common-shape, measurable-nuisance benchmark. Classical fixed-support regression yields a lower endpoint but cannot decide whether a certificate-induced window restriction is unavoidable.
fill: A finite-sample uniformly honest bracket separates the complete-data frontier from the buffered-extrema upper transition. The explicit wider-window grid certificate starts an upper route without adding a class assumption; joint support-and-nuisance testing supplies the lower route. Both routes concern \(\mathcal M_n\) with \(C^3\) responses subject only to \(G_1\) and \(G_3\). The response class is a strict subclass of the published H\"older seminorm class, closed under arbitrary intercept shifts, and no width exponent is assumed in class membership.
